p.src: Now Wang Qing was staying at Gong Duan’s manor in Gong Family Village. One cool morning, as the bright sun began to rise and a gentle breeze stirred, he was beneath the willows by the threshing ground, instructing the Gong brothers in punches and kicks. Suddenly, a burly man swaggered in. His head was bare, with no scarf or cap, and his hair was tied in a topknot. He wore a short, open-fronted jacket of fine Leizhou ramie, a single-gauze skirt, and a pair of straw sandals. Holding a small triangular cattail fan, he strode in with his face raised and his hands clasped behind his back, and saw that an exiled convict was giving instruction there. The day before, he had already heard that an exiled convict in Mangdong Town had defeated a man skilled with spear and staff. Fearing that the Gong brothers might learn his secrets, he began abusing Wang Qing: “You are a condemned criminal! How dare you loiter on the road instead of completing your journey and come here to deceive another family’s sons?” Wang Qing assumed that he was a kinsman of the Gong family and dared not answer. This man was none other than Huang Da of East Village. Taking advantage of the cool morning, he was on his way to collect a gambling debt from Liu Dalang at the western end of Gong Family Village. Hearing shouts and cries from Gong Duan’s village, and being accustomed to bullying the Gong brothers, he had barged straight in. When Gong Duan saw that it was Huang Da, a nameless fire of fury flared three thousand fathoms high in his breast. Unable to restrain himself, he cursed: “You thieving bastard, spawned by donkeys and oxen! The other day you refused to pay me my gambling winnings, and today you come to my door to bully me again!” Huang Da flew into a rage and shouted: “Damn your mother’s guts!” He threw down his cattail fan, raised his fists, rushed forward, and struck straight at Gong Duan’s face. From their exchange Wang Qing guessed that the man was Huang Da. Pretending to step forward to make peace, he swung his cangue and struck Huang Da on the shoulder. With a thud Huang Da toppled heels over head. Before he could struggle up, Gong Duan, Gong Zheng, and two farmhands rushed forward together and pinned him down. Fists and toes rained upon his back, chest, shoulder blades, ribs, arms, cheeks, brow, and limbs; not a spot escaped their blows, and only the tip of his tongue remained free. They kicked and beat Huang Da without count, tearing his ramie jacket and gauze skirt to shreds. Huang Da merely cried out: “Good beating! Good beating!” When not a single thread remained upon his stark-naked body, the escort officers Sun Lin and He Ji repeatedly intervened, and only then did Gong Duan and the others stop. They had beaten Huang Da senseless. He could only lie on the ground gasping; how could he possibly struggle to his feet? Gong Duan ordered three or four farmhands to carry Huang Da to a patch of grass halfway to East Village and cast him down there, leaving him beneath the blazing sun for half the day. Some neighboring farmers from Huang Da’s village came out to weed their fields and happened upon him. They helped him home, where he took to his bed to recover. He asked someone to write a complaint and submit it to Xin’an County, reporting the assault and reserving judgment should he die. But of this no more need be said.

p.src: Meanwhile, after Gong Duan and the others had spent the whole morning in that uproar, they ordered the farmhands to bring out food and wine and invited Wang Qing and his companions to breakfast. Wang Qing said: “That fellow is certain to return for revenge and cause trouble.” Gong Duan replied: “That thieving bastard is as poor as can be and has only a wife at home. His neighbors tolerate him only because of his strength. Now that they have seen the thieving bastard beaten senseless, they certainly will not exert themselves on his behalf. If he dies, I will sacrifice one farmhand to pay for his life. Even if it means a lawsuit, nothing can be done about it. If he does not die, it will be nothing more than a lawsuit over a mutual brawl. Today, Master, it was entirely thanks to you that we avenged ourselves. Have a cup of wine and remain here without worry. Please teach us brothers all the arts of spear and staff as well, and we shall certainly repay your kindness.” Gong Duan brought out two silver ingots, each weighing five taels, and gave them to the two officers, asking them to allow a few more days. Having received the money, Sun Lin and He Ji could only agree. They remained there for more than ten days in succession, during which Wang Qing passed on all the essential techniques of spear and staff to Gong Duan and Gong Zheng. When the officers pressed them to depart, and news also came that Huang Da had sent someone to the county and obtained leave to bring his complaint, Gong Duan took out fifty taels of silver and gave it to Wang Qing for his expenses in Shanzhou. They rose in the middle of the night, packed their baggage and bundles, and left the manor before dawn. Gong Duan told his brother to take some silver and accompany them once more as an escort. Nothing of note occurred on the road, and in no more than a day they reached Shanzhou. Sun Lin and He Ji took Wang Qing to the prefectural office and submitted the Kaifeng Prefecture dispatch in the main hall. The prefect examined everything and found it in order. He took Wang Qing into custody and issued a written receipt for the two officers to carry back. But of them no more need be said. The prefect at once issued an order assigning Wang Qing to the local prison camp. The officers there counted him in, took charge of him, and reported back; this too need not be related.

p.src: Before he knew it, two months had passed, and the season had advanced into late autumn. One day, while Wang Qing was sitting idly in the single men’s quarters, a soldier came in and said: “The superintendent summons you.” Wang Qing followed the soldier to the inspection hall and kowtowed. The superintendent, Zhang Shikai, said: “You have been here a long while, yet I have never assigned you any task. I wish to buy a fine horn bow from Chenzhou. Chenzhou lies under the jurisdiction of the Eastern Capital, and since you are a man of the Eastern Capital, you must know the prices and how to distinguish genuine wares from false ones.” When he had finished speaking, he drew a paper packet from his sleeve, handed it personally to Wang Qing, and said: “Here are two taels of fine silver. Go buy the bow and report back.” Wang Qing replied: “Your servant understands.” He took the silver back to his quarters and opened the paper packet. The silver was indeed pure and white as snow; when he weighed it on a small balance, it was actually three or four candareens overweight. Wang Qing left the camp and went to an archery shop in the market on the street north of the prefectural seat. There he spent only one tael and seven mace of silver to buy a genuine Chenzhou horn bow. When he brought it back, Superintendent Zhang was no longer in the hall. Wang Qing handed the bow to a personal attendant from the inner residence to take inside, pleased that he had gained three mace of silver from the errand. The next day Zhang Shikai again summoned Wang Qing to the inspection hall and said: “You are indeed capable. The horn bow you bought yesterday is excellent.” Wang Qing said: “My lord, you must have a fire kept in the bow cabinet and warm it continually; only then will it remain in good condition.” Zhang Shikai replied: “I know that.” From then on, Zhang Shikai sent Wang Qing out every day to purchase food and other supplies. Unlike the first time, however, he no longer gave him ready silver. Instead he handed him an account book and ordered him to record in it everything he bought each day. But which of the merchants and shopkeepers would extend him so much as half a copper coin in credit? Wang Qing had no choice but to take out his own money, buy the goods, and deliver them inside the government compound. Zhang Shikai found fault whether the goods were good or bad and either beat or cursed him. When ten days had passed, Wang Qing presented the account book and requested reimbursement, but not the slightest sum was issued to him. This continued for more than a month. Superintendent Zhang had him beaten sometimes five strokes, sometimes ten, sometimes twenty, and sometimes thirty. All told, he received more than three hundred strokes, until both legs were beaten raw. And the fifty taels of silver Gong Duan had given him were entirely consumed by these expenses.

p.src: One day, Wang Qing went to the shop of Physician Zhang, on the east side of the Martial Merit Arch west of the camp. The doctor compounded pills and powders, sold prepared medicinal slices, treated both internal and external ailments, dispensed ready-made medicines, and also sold salves for cudgel wounds. Wang Qing bought several plasters there and applied them to his injuries. As Physician Zhang applied the plasters, he said, “Commandant Zhang’s brother-in-law, Young Master Pang, also came here the other day for a plaster for his right wrist. He said he had hurt it in a fall at Mangdong Town, but when I looked at his wrist, it seemed to have been injured by a blow.” Hearing this, Wang Qing hurriedly asked, “I am in the camp, so why have I never seen him?” Physician Zhang replied, “He is the younger full brother of Commandant Zhang’s junior wife, and his personal name is Yuan. Madam Pang is Commandant Zhang’s favorite. Young Master Pang loves gambling and also enjoys playing with spears and staves. Fortunately for him, that sister of his is always looking after him.” After hearing all this, Wang Qing was almost certain that the fellow he had beaten beneath the cypress tree the other day must have been Pang Yuan. No wonder Zhang Shikai had been looking for a pretext to punish and torment him. Wang Qing took leave of Physician Zhang and returned to the camp. In secret he treated one of the commandant’s personal attendants to wine and meat, gave him money, and gradually drew from him the full particulars about Pang Yuan. p.src: Then one day Commandant Zhang again ordered him to buy two bolts of satin. With his worries weighing on him, Wang Qing dared not be negligent. He hurried to the shop, made the purchase, and returned to the camp. Commandant Zhang was seated in the inspection hall, and Wang Qing went forward to report. Zhang Shikai complained that the satin’s color was poor, its measure too short, and its pattern outmoded. He immediately cursed Wang Qing: “You insolent slave! You are a convict and ought by rights to be sent to carry water and move stones, or else be chained to the great fetters. Sending you on errands today is showing you the greatest favor. Yet you wretched rogue cannot tell kindness from ill treatment!” Wang Qing was berated into speechlessness and kowtowed as rapidly as if he were setting candles in place, begging for mercy. Zhang Shikai shouted, “For now I shall leave one cudgeling on your account. Go at once and exchange the satin for good cloth. You must report back tonight. If you are delayed in the least, take good care of that miserable life of yours!” Wang Qing had no choice but to take off the clothes he wore, pawn them at a pawnshop for two strings of cash, add that money to the price, and exchange the cloth for fine satin, which he carried back to the camp. After all his trudging, the lamps had already been lit, and he found the camp gate closed. The soldier on duty said, “Who would take responsibility for letting you in after dark?” Wang Qing explained, “His Honor our commandant sent me on this errand.” But how could the soldier on duty be persuaded to listen? Wang Qing still had some money left, and only after giving it to the guards did they let him in, though they harried him for some time more. Carrying the two bolts of satin, he came to the gate of the inner residence. The keeper of the inner gate said, “His Honor the commandant quarreled with the senior wife and has gone to the junior wife’s room at the rear. The senior wife is fearsome indeed. Who would dare carry a message for you and invite trouble?” Wang Qing thought, “He ordered me to report tonight, so why do they obstruct me like this? Is this not a deliberate scheme to harm me? How can I escape that vicious cudgeling tomorrow? My life will surely be lost at the hands of that damned cuckold. He has had me beaten more than three hundred strokes; that should be more than enough repayment for the grudge over that one blow. Besides, he previously accepted so much silver from Gong Zheng, yet today he turns against me and torments me so cruelly!”

p.src: Wang Qing had been vicious and defiant from childhood; even his own parents never dared provoke him twice. Now his rebellious temper flared. Saying to himself, “He who does not avenge the smallest wrong is no gentleman; he who lacks ruthlessness is no true man,” he resolved to go through with it once and for all. He waited until after the night watch, when everyone in the camp and all the prisoners were asleep, then quietly slipped behind the inner residence, climbed over the wall, gently drew the bolt from the rear gate, and hid to one side. By the starlight he saw a stable against the eastern wall and a small hut to the west. On inspection, it proved to be a privy over a cesspit. Wang Qing lifted a wooden hurdle from the stable and stood it against the wall by the second gate. He climbed it to the top of the wall, hauled the hurdle up after him, lowered it upright on the inner side, and quietly slid down. First he drew the bolt of the second gate and hid the wooden hurdle. There was yet another wall within, and from beyond it he heard loud laughter and conversation. Wang Qing crept to the wall, crouched, and listened closely. He recognized Zhang Shikai’s voice, a woman’s voice, and another man’s voice; they were drinking and chatting inside. After eavesdropping for a long while, Wang Qing suddenly heard Zhang Shikai say, “Brother-in-law, when that fellow comes to report tomorrow, his life will end beneath the cudgel.” Then he heard the other man say, “I have nearly finished reckoning up the possessions that fellow carries. Brother-in-law, you must make up your mind to strike for me and let me vent this accursed rage!” Zhang Shikai replied, “Within a day or two I shall see that you have your satisfaction!” The woman said, “Surely that is enough! You two must let the matter rest!” The man said, “What are you saying, sister? Stay out of it!” Outside the wall, Wang Qing heard the three of them speaking in turn and understood everything clearly. Rage filled his heart, and the nameless fire of wrath within him shot three thousand fathoms high. Unable to restrain himself, he wished he possessed the divine strength of a vajra, so that he might push down the plastered wall, charge inside, and kill the lot of them. Just so it is said:

Unable to restrain himself, he wished he possessed the divine strength of a vajra, so that he might push down the plastered wall, charge inside, and kill the lot of them.
Just so it is said:

p.src: Too many delights upon the tongue will end in sickness; once a pleasing deed is done, calamity must follow. Before the autumn wind has stirred, the cicada senses it; but when impermanence comes secretly, how can one guard against it?

p.src: Wang Qing could restrain himself no longer when he heard Zhang Shikai call loudly, “Boy, light a lamp and take me to the privy at the back.” At these words, Wang Qing hurriedly drew the sharp knife he carried for protection and crouched in a huddle behind the plum tree. Then, with a creak, the two leaves of the inner gate opened. Watching from the darkness, Wang Qing saw the very servant boy who had been secretly passing him news each day come out carrying a lantern, with Zhang Shikai striding behind him. Unaware that anyone lurked in the shadows, Zhang Shikai walked straight ahead until he reached the second gate, where he cursed, “What careless slaves! Why have they left this bolt undone so late at night?” The boy opened the gate and held up the light. No sooner had Zhang Shikai passed through the second gate than Wang Qing silently edged up behind him. Hearing footsteps behind him, Zhang Shikai turned his head and saw Wang Qing rushing forward, a knife drawn in his right hand and the five fingers of his left spread wide. Zhang Shikai’s heart and every organ in his body seemed to fly beyond the highest clouds, and he cried, “A thief!” Before the words were fully spoken, Wang Qing’s blade had already fallen, striking Zhang Shikai beside the ear and cutting deep into his neck. He toppled to the ground. Though the boy knew Wang Qing well from ordinary days, how could he not be terrified now that he saw him committing murder with a gleaming knife in his hand? He tried to flee, but his feet seemed nailed to the ground; and when he tried to cry out, his mouth seemed struck dumb and no sound would come. He stood utterly petrified with fear. As Zhang Shikai struggled for life, Wang Qing caught up and stabbed him once more squarely in the back, putting an end to him. Pang Yuan was drinking in his elder sister’s room. Hearing faint cries outside, he hastily lit a lamp and ran out to see what was happening. Seeing someone coming from within, Wang Qing kicked the lantern-bearing boy. Boy and lantern went tumbling together, and the flame was extinguished. Pang Yuan assumed that Zhang Shikai was beating the boy and called, “Brother-in-law, why are you beating that lad?” He was just stepping forward to intervene when Wang Qing sprang at him and, in the darkness, thrust his blade straight into Pang Yuan’s ribs; Pang Yuan gave a squeal like a slaughtered pig and pitched to the ground. Wang Qing seized him by the hair and cut off his head with one stroke. Hearing the dreadful cries outside, Madam Pang hurriedly ordered her maids to light a lamp, then came out with them to investigate. When Wang Qing saw Madam Pang emerge, he moved forward to kill her as well. But what an extraordinary thing then occurred! You would scarcely believe it if it were told. In the blink of an eye, Wang Qing saw more than a dozen personal attendants behind Madam Pang, all brandishing weapons as they rushed out shouting. Thrown into confusion, Wang Qing dashed outside, opened the rear gate, and scaled the compound’s back wall. He stripped off his bloodstained clothes, wiped his knife clean, and concealed it on his person. The watch drum told him it was already the third watch. Taking advantage of the silent streets, Wang Qing made his way toward the city wall. Shanzhou was an earthen-walled city whose ramparts were not very high and whose moat was not very deep, so that very night Wang Qing climbed over the wall and escaped.

p.src: Let us leave Wang Qing after he crossed the city wall and speak instead of Zhang Shikai’s concubine, Madam Pang. In truth, she had come out with only two maids carrying a lamp; no attendants had accompanied her at all. First she saw her brother Pang Yuan’s blood-drenched head lying on one side and his body on the other. Madam Pang and the maids stared at one another in horror, as though their skulls had been split into eight pieces and half a bucket of icy snow-water poured inside. For a long while none could speak. Then Madam Pang and the two maids stumbled and tumbled back inside, trembling all over. They raised the alarm and summoned the personal attendants within and the guards on duty outside, who lit torches, seized weapons, and all went to inspect the rear courtyard. Outside the second gate they found Commandant Zhang murdered as well. The servant boy lay fallen on the ground, still struggling for breath and vomiting blood; plainly he could not survive. Seeing the rear gate open, everyone assumed the killer had come from behind. They surged outside to investigate and, by the torchlight, saw two bolts of colored silk discarded on the ground. With one voice they declared that Wang Qing was the culprit. They hurriedly counted all the prisoners and found that Wang Qing alone was missing. The entire compound was thrown into an uproar, as were all the neighboring households on every side. Beyond the rear wall they illuminated the bloodstained garments and examined them closely; every piece belonged to Wang Qing. They all conferred and decided that, before the city gates opened, they must report to the prefect and have men dispatched at once to search for and arrest him. By then it was already the fifth watch. The prefect was greatly alarmed by the report and immediately sent the county military officer to examine the dead, determine their number, and investigate where the murderer had entered and escaped; at the same time, he ordered all four gates of Shanzhou tightly closed, mustered soldiers and arresting officers, and commanded the ward headmen throughout the city to search every house for the murderer Wang Qing. The gates remained shut amid turmoil for two days, while every family and every household was searched in turn, yet no trace of him was found. The prefect issued sealed documents and appointed officials to order the local constables and village heads throughout the jurisdiction to search house by house and capture the chief culprit. The notices listed Wang Qing’s native place, age, features, and appearance, included a drawn likeness, and offered a confirmed reward of one thousand strings of cash. Anyone who learned Wang Qing’s whereabouts and reported them to the prefecture would receive the stated reward; but anyone who concealed the fugitive in his home and provided him with food or lodging would, upon discovery and prosecution, suffer the same punishment as the criminal. These orders were circulated throughout the neighboring prefectures and counties so that all might join in the pursuit.

p.src: Now Wang Qing climbed out of Shanzhou city that very night. Gathering up his clothes, he crossed the moat at a shallow place and reached the opposite bank. He thought to himself, “Though I have escaped with my life, where can I go to hide?” It was nearly midwinter; the leaves had fallen and the grass had withered, and by starlight he could make out the paths. That night Wang Qing turned down three or four narrow lanes before at last reaching a main road. He hurried onward until the red sun rose in the east. Having covered some sixty or seventy li, he was traveling south when he saw ahead a densely settled place. Wang Qing reflected that he still had a string of cash on him. He would first go there and buy something to eat and drink, then decide where to seek refuge. Before long he reached the marketplace. It was still early, and the wine shops and meat stalls had not yet opened. Only beneath the eaves of an east-facing house hung a battered lantern advertising lodging for travelers. The household had neglected to take it in the previous night, and the door still stood half open. Wang Qing stepped forward and pushed the door open with a creak. Inside, he saw a man who had not yet washed or combed his hair coming out from the rear. When Wang Qing looked closely, he recognized the man as Fan Quan, a prison warden and a maternal cousin of his. From childhood, Fan Quan had followed his father in conducting profitable business in Fangzhou, and had subsequently become a jail sergeant overseeing the two prisons of that prefecture. In the third month of that spring he had gone to the Eastern Capital on official business and had stayed several days at Wang Qing’s home. Wang Qing immediately called out, “Elder brother, I trust you have been well since we last met!” Fan Quan replied, “You look like Brother Wang Qing.” But seeing his appearance and the two lines of penal brands tattooed on his face, Fan Quan was filled with doubt and had yet to give a proper response. Seeing no one nearby, Wang Qing suddenly dropped to his knees and said, “Elder brother, please save me!” Fan Quan hurriedly helped him up and said, “Are you truly Brother Wang Qing?” Wang Qing waved his hand and said, “Keep your voice down!” Understanding at once, Fan Quan seized Wang Qing by the sleeve and pulled him into the guest room. As it happened, Fan Quan had rented a private room for himself the night before. Fan Quan quietly asked in haste, “Brother, how did you come to look like this?” Wang Qing whispered in his ear, recounting how he had become entangled in a criminal case and been tattooed and banished to Shanzhou. He then told how Zhang Shikai had pursued his revenge with savage cruelty, and described everything that had happened the night before. Fan Quan was greatly alarmed when he had heard the whole account. After hesitating for a while, he hurriedly washed, dressed, and ate, settled the charges for the room and meal, and arranged for Wang Qing to pose as an attendant traveling with the prison officer. They left the inn and set out for Fangzhou. On the road, Wang Qing asked why Fan Quan had come there. Fan Quan replied, “Our prefect sent me to deliver a letter to the prefect of Shanzhou. I obtained his reply only yesterday and left Shanzhou at once, but as night had fallen, I lodged here. I had no idea that you were in Shanzhou, still less that you had done such a thing.” Fan Quan and Wang Qing rested by day and traveled by night, secretly fleeing to Fangzhou. Only two days later, Shanzhou issued an official circular ordering the search and arrest of the criminal Wang Qing. Fan Quan broke into a cold sweat. Returning home, he informed Wang Qing and said, “You certainly cannot remain safely within the city. East of Dingshan Fort outside the city, I have several thatched cottages and more than twenty mu of farmland, which I bought the year before last. Several farmhands are cultivating it now. Go there and hide for a few days, brother, and afterward we shall decide what to do.” After nightfall, Fan Quan led Wang Qing out of the city and hid him in a thatched cottage east of Dingshan Fort. He also changed Wang Qing’s name and surname, calling him Li De. Fan Quan worried that the penal brands on Wang Qing’s face would endanger him. Fortunately, when he had visited Jiankang years before, he had heard of the fame of An Daoquan, the “Divine Physician.” By cultivating his friendship with generous gifts, Fan Quan had learned a method for treating penal brands. He applied a caustic drug to remove Wang Qing’s tattoos, then treated him with fine medicine. After the wounds formed red scars, he applied a preparation of finely powdered gold and jade. In a little over two months, even the scars had faded away.

p.src: Time slipped swiftly by. More than a hundred days passed, and it was now the middle month of spring in the first year of Xuanhe. The authorities’ search had begun with a tiger’s head but ended with a snake’s tail: fierce at first, it had gradually slackened. With the penal brands gone from his face, Wang Qing gradually began venturing outside. Fan Quan supplied all his clothes, shoes, and socks. One day, as Wang Qing sat bored in the thatched cottage, he suddenly heard the distant din of a boisterous crowd. Wang Qing went out and asked a farmhand what was causing such excitement. The farmhand replied, “Master Li, perhaps you do not know that a little more than one li west of here lies the Duan family estate within Dingshan Fort. The Duan brothers have invited a singing girl to this prefecture and erected a stage on which she performs all manner of songs and musical pieces. She is a newly arrived courtesan from the Western Capital, peerless in both beauty and artistry, and crowds as vast as mountains and seas have come to see her. Why not go there and take a look, master?” Once Wang Qing heard this, how could he possibly keep his feet still? He went straight to Dingshan Fort. Because Wang Qing came to this place, a banished convict would be joined in marriage to a village woman, while a local tyrant would become a scourge upon the whole region. Whether Wang Qing truly found a singing girl performing when he went there to watch will be revealed in the next chapter.
